accessibility.method: axe-core 4.10.2 (wcag2a/wcag2aa/wcag21a/wcag21aa) on rendered DOM, two pages

homepage.topIssue: select-name (critical): the course-search 'study level' <select> has no accessible name

accessibility.note: Automated axe scan only — covers ~30-40% of WCAG success criteria; manual keyboard/screen-reader testing not performed. The single homepage violation is a real, high-value fix (unlabeled form control on the primary conversion widget).

scorecard.note: accessibility + performance now measured (see measurements.accessibility / measurements.coreWebVitals); technical-seo still nulled this pass. accessibility 85 = strong automated result (27 passes, 1 critical select-name on homepage) but axe covers only a subset of WCAG; performance 90 = all Core Web Vitals pass on both viewports (unthrottled lab). overall is the mean of the six scored dimensions.

findings.evidence: Source palette measured as navy #18194f / blue #3860be / green #68b631 accent; project styles/brand.css uses --uon-navy #10263b + --uon-gold #deb406 (no blue/green). Gold stat panels + pink interior CTAs are present on the source but not tokenized in brand.css.
findings.businessImpact: Migrated pages will read as on-brand-ish but not pixel-faithful to the live site; the pink primary-CTA and gold stat treatments are load-bearing brand signals.
findings.fix: Reconcile styles/brand.css tokens with the measured source palette: confirm the exact navy, add the pink/magenta primary-CTA token and the gold stat-panel token as first-class variables; decide whether the green accent is in-scope.

findings.evidence: Interior pages (international-applicants) use a two-CTA action bar (pink primary pill + navy secondary pill) repeated top and bottom; a testimonial quote in a navy keyline box; a 5-up star-ranking strip. None of these exact patterns exist as blocks (nearest: cards-icon-light, cards-ranking-gold).
findings.businessImpact: Without these blocks, interior study pages fall back to default content or approximate blocks, losing the source's clear primary/secondary action hierarchy.
findings.fix: Add 3 blocks: cta-bar-dual (pink+navy pill action bar), quote-testimonial-dark (keyline quote), cards-stars-ranking (5-up star stat strip) OR extend cards-ranking-gold with a star/icon option.

findings.evidence: Body CTA vocabulary is already consistent and verb-led across pages (measurements.ctaVocabulary). The homepage course-search + gold ranking stats + promo grid is a strong, reusable conversion pattern already covered by search-course-light + cards-ranking-gold + cards-promo-dark-withimg-4.
findings.businessImpact: Low risk — the highest-traffic conversion surfaces map cleanly to existing blocks.
findings.fix: No new block needed; reuse the existing homepage/study-hub block set.

findings.evidence: Key facts (rankings '1st / Top 20 / Top 100', open-day dates) render as text on the homepage (good), but on interior pages several stats sit inside star-icon graphics; Scene7 imagery is heavily used. No llms.txt observed at origin root (not fetched this pass).
findings.businessImpact: Answer engines may miss ranking/stat claims locked in icon graphics; strong, citable prose exists on international-applicants (29k chars) which is good.
findings.fix: Ensure the star-ranking block renders figure + caption as text (not baked into images); consider an llms.txt at the EDS site root during rollout.

findings.evidence: Source IA is .aspx-heavy with cert issues on a subtree (opticord/* returned ERR_CERT_COMMON_NAME_INVALID) and 404s on guessed pillar URLs (research/business/about .aspx). The migration's import scripts already handle .aspx→clean-path (documented fix); shared header/footer chrome inflates every page.
findings.businessImpact: Clean-URL migration is a real SEO win vs the legacy .aspx structure; but redirects from legacy .aspx URLs must be planned or link equity is lost.
findings.fix: Plan a redirect map (legacy .aspx → clean EDS path) as part of rollout; the .aspx path-normalization already lives in the import scripts.

findings.evidence: axe-core 4.10.2 (wcag2a/aa, 2.1a/aa) on the live homepage: 1 critical violation, rule `select-name` — the course-search 'study level' <select> (options: Undergraduate, Postgraduate, Research opportunities, Apprenticeships, Online, Preparatory English) has no accessible name. Interior page (international-applicants) scanned clean (0 violations, 27 passes).
findings.businessImpact: The unlabeled control is on the homepage's primary conversion widget (course search); screen-reader users can't tell what the dropdown selects, directly excluding users at the top of the enrolment funnel.
findings.fix: Give the study-level <select> an accessible name — an associated <label>, or aria-label="Select study level". In the migrated EDS search-course-light block, ensure the select renders with a label/aria-label; this is a one-line fix that clears the only critical automated a11y issue found.

findings.evidence: In-session Playwright lab (unthrottled): desktop 1440x900 LCP 1720ms / CLS 0 / TBT-proxy 214ms across 63 resources ~4.4MB; mobile 375x667 LCP 1260ms / CLS 0.014 / TBT-proxy 229ms. All three Core Web Vitals pass Google 'good' thresholds on both viewports (measurements.coreWebVitals).
findings.businessImpact: Low risk — the source already meets CWV in the lab. The migration should hold or improve this (EDS is built for CWV); the ~4.4MB desktop transfer is the main headroom.
findings.fix: No action required to pass; treat as a floor to protect. Validate a throttled PSI/field INP reading during rollout, and keep desktop transfer weight in check (image optimization, defer non-critical JS) — EDS's eager/lazy/delayed phasing already targets this.

quote-testimonial-dark — testimonial quote in a navy keyline box

4. Plan legacy .aspx → clean-path redirect map for rollout (F5).
